frequency_question: What proportion of these attempts achieve operational status within the specified timeframe when preceded by observable preparatory precursor signals?
membership_rule: Includes state-level programs attempting to establish domestic final assembly, component manufacture, or maintenance-to-production conversion for foreign-designed cruise missiles or heavy precision munitions during wartime. Excludes simple technology transfers without domestic manufacturing setup.

cases.name: Ukraine domestic production attempt of Neptune/Hrim derivatives
Taiwan domestic production scale-up of Hsiung Feng missiles
Iran domestic reverse-engineering and assembly of Soumar/Qods cruise missiles
Pakistan domestic production of Babur cruise missile series
South Korea domestic mass production of Hyunmoo cruise/ballistic variants
Ukraine attempt to domesticate Western air-defense missile components (FrankenSAM)

provenance_note: rate of 100% from only 6 case(s); too few to establish an extreme base rate -- treat as directional
coverage_note: 6 named; representative of the constrained class of high-priority wartime missile domestication efforts.
known_gaps: Classified or highly covert bilateral co-production arrangements between states are difficult to fully verify in real-time.
skeleton: 6 observed wartime advanced missile domestic production or major co-production programs across constrained state actors, yielding operational lines within short timeframes when external technical assistance is present.
multiplier: 6 hits out of 6 documented comparable cases with similar technical assistance and urgency.
validity_reason: The base rate reflects enduring engineering and wartime necessity dynamics that remain stable through the current decade.
